case_title: SHAILENDRA RAJDEV PASVAN v. STATE OF GUJARAT ETC.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.21(1)(a); Indian Explosives Act ss.3, 5
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that on 4th February 2001, the complainant's son, who was about 9 years old, went missing. The complainant initially joined the search for his son but later disappeared. The complainant later received an extra-judicial confession from one of the accused, who claimed to have kidnapped the son and handed him over to others. The body of the missing child was found in an agricultural field several days later. The prosecution's case relied heavily on circumstantial evidence and the theory of last seen, but the trial court acquitted the accused due to contradictions in the evidence and lack of direct proof. The High Court overturned the acquittal, but the Supreme Court ultimately set aside the conviction, finding the evidence insufficient to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.
